name: Alisher Usmanov
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found; at age 26 he was jailed for fraud and served six years in prison, with his business career beginning only after his release in 1986.
early_history_summary: Born in Chust, Uzbekistan, to a state prosecutor father, Usmanov graduated from MGIMO in 1976 with a law degree. At age 26 he was convicted of fraud and theft of socialist property, serving six years of an eight-year sentence before his release in 1986. His business career began in the late 1980s with a plastic-bag cooperative.
family_context_summary: Born to a state prosecutor father in Uzbekistan; family was relatively privileged within the Soviet system. Father was deputy prosecutor general for Tashkent.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a state prosecutor; no business or commercial domain expertise documented in the family.
evidence_summary: Usmanov graduated from MGIMO in 1976 but was imprisoned at age 26 for fraud, serving six years. His wealth was built in the post-Soviet era through metals, mining, and technology investments, beginning with a cooperative in the late 1980s. No material business milestone occurred by age 26.

name: Todd McFarlane
milestone_by_age_26: Hired as a freelance artist by Marvel Comics around 1984-1985, and by age 26 was drawing mainstream titles for both Marvel and DC including Incredible Hulk and Detective Comics.
early_history_summary: McFarlane began drawing comics at age 16 in Calgary, largely self-taught by studying favorite artists. He attended Eastern Washington University on a baseball scholarship while working as a janitor and at a comic shop, drawing late at night. After graduation in 1984, he was hired by Marvel on a freelance basis after accumulating hundreds of rejection letters.
primary_leverage_engine: Self-taught artistic skill and relentless persistence
family_context_summary: Born to Bob and Sherlee McFarlane in Calgary; father worked in the printing business, causing the family to move frequently. Not wealthy; McFarlane worked multiple jobs through college.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father worked in the printing business, providing some tangential connection to graphics and publishing, but no direct comics industry transfer.
primary_early_advantage_tags: self-taught, comic shop exposure, printing family, relentless practice
evidence_summary: McFarlane started drawing comics at 16, self-taught by studying favorite artists. He worked as a janitor and at a comic shop while at EWU on a baseball scholarship, drawing late at night. After 700+ rejection letters, he was hired by Marvel around 1984-85. His father's printing business gave tangential exposure to graphics. A baseball injury forced his pivot from sports to comics full-time. By 26 he was a professional artist at Marvel and DC.
starting_point: Born to a working-class family in Calgary, Alberta; father worked in the printing business, causing the family to relocate frequently between Alberta and California.
current_position: President and co-founder of Image Comics; creator of Spawn; runs McFarlane Toys; estimated net worth ~$300M; resides in Arizona.

trajectory.event: Hired as a freelance artist by Marvel Comics after years of rejection letters and self-taught practice.
Assigned to pencil Marvel's flagship title The Amazing Spider-Man starting with issue 298, transforming the character's visual style.
His Spider-Man work became the best-selling comic book issue of all time, selling 2.5 million copies.
Co-founded Image Comics and launched Spawn, whose debut issue sold 1.7 million copies, a record for an independent comic.
Produced the Spawn live-action film adaptation starring Michael Jai White.
Named National Football League Artist of the Year; expanded McFarlane Toys into a major collectibles brand.

name: Hryhorii Chapkis
milestone_by_age_26: Joined the State Ensemble of Song and Dance of Ukraine as a professional ballet dancer in February 1946 at age 16, and became a choreographer at the Ivan Franko Theatre by age 20.
early_history_summary: Born in Chișinău in a large family of seven children, Chapkis began dancing at age 10 on the streets. During WWII his family was evacuated to Kazakhstan, then settled in Kyiv. He entered a choreographic studio at the Kyiv Opera Theatre in 1943 and joined the State Ensemble of Song and Dance of Ukraine in 1946, touring over 70 countries.
primary_leverage_engine: Early immersion in dance and state ensemble pipeline
family_context_summary: Born into a large, poor family in Chișinău (then Kingdom of Romania); mother was a homemaker, father's occupation not documented. Family evacuated during WWII to Kazakhstan, then Kyiv.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources; no evidence of family dance or artistic background.
primary_early_advantage_tags: wartime hardship, street dancing, state ensemble, choreographic studio, early start
evidence_summary: Chapkis grew up in poverty in a large family in Chișinău, learning dance informally on the streets from age 10. WWII forced evacuation to Kazakhstan and then Kyiv, where he entered a choreographic studio at the Kyiv Opera Theatre at 13. He joined the State Ensemble of Song and Dance of Ukraine at 16, becoming a professional dancer. By 20 he was a choreographer at the Ivan Franko Theatre. His early career was shaped by wartime adversity and the Soviet state cultural pipeline.
starting_point: Born into a large, poor family in Chișinău, Moldova (then Kingdom of Romania); one of seven children; mother was a homemaker; family evacuated during WWII.
current_position: Died on June 13, 2021, at age 91 in Kyiv, Ukraine; final role was professor at Kyiv National University of Culture and Arts and judge on Dancing with the Stars Ukraine.

trajectory.event: Entered the choreographic studio at the Kyiv Opera Theatre under B.A. Dolidze during wartime.
Joined the State Ensemble of Song and Dance of Ukraine as a professional ballet dancer.
Became a choreographer at the Ivan Franko Theatre in Kyiv.
Began performing with the State Dance Ensemble of the Ukrainian SSR under Pavlo Virsky, touring over 70 countries.
Awarded the title of Meritorious Artist of the Ukrainian SSR.
Transitioned to ballroom choreography and became advisor to the Council for Ballroom Dance at the Ukrainian Ministry of Culture.
Awarded People's Artist of Ukraine.
Died on June 13, 2021, in Kyiv.

name: Jarno Trulli
milestone_by_age_26: Won the Karting World Championship in 1991 at age 17, then won the German Formula Three Championship in 1996 and made his Formula One debut with Minardi in 1997 at age 23.
early_history_summary: Born in Pescara, Italy, to a modest family, Trulli started karting at age 8, driven by his motorsport-fan father Enzo. He won the Karting World Championship at 17, progressed to German F3 where he won the 1996 title, and jumped to Formula One with Minardi in 1997, quickly being poached by Prost mid-season.
primary_leverage_engine: Physical talent and early racing specialization
family_context_summary: Born to a modest family in Pescara, Italy; father Enzo was a motorsport fan who set up a kart team with friends and took time off work to support Jarno's racing ambitions.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a passionate motorsport fan who introduced Jarno to karting at age 8, set up a local kart team, and traveled to races; no professional racing background in the family.
primary_early_advantage_tags: father as mentor, karting from age 8, Italian motorsport culture, early world championship, Benetton backing
evidence_summary: Trulli was born to a modest family in Pescara, Italy. His father Enzo, a motorsport fan, introduced him to karting at age 8 and set up a local team with friends. Trulli showed immediate talent, driving like a 14-15 year old at age 8-9. He won the Karting World Championship at 17, the German F3 title at 22, and debuted in Formula One at 23 with Minardi. His father took time off work and traveled by van to support his racing career.
starting_point: Born to a modest family in Pescara, Italy; father Enzo was a motorsport fan who introduced him to karting and supported his early career.
current_position: Retired from Formula One after the 2011 season; co-owner of a vineyard in Abruzzo (Poderi Castorani); produces Trulli Kart brand; resides in Lugano, Switzerland.

trajectory.event: Won the Karting World Championship, establishing himself as one of karting's top talents.
Won the German Formula Three Championship with KMS, backed by Opel and the Benetton F1 team.
Made Formula One debut with Minardi; mid-season replaced injured Olivier Panis at Prost, impressing immediately with a fourth-place finish in Germany.
Scored his first F1 podium with second place at the European Grand Prix in wet conditions.
Won the Monaco Grand Prix with Renault, his sole F1 victory, from pole position.
Delivered Toyota's first-ever F1 podium finishes and helped the team to fourth in the Constructors' Championship.
Retired from Formula One after competing for Team Lotus/Caterham, ending a 15-season F1 career with 256 entries.

name: 50 Cent
milestone_by_age_26: Signed to Columbia Records and recorded the album Power of the Dollar in 1999-2000, with the single 'How to Rob' generating significant industry buzz and responses from Jay-Z, Ghostface Killah, and Wyclef Jean.
early_history_summary: Born Curtis Jackson III in Queens, New York, 50 Cent was raised by his grandparents after his drug-dealer mother was murdered when he was 8. He dealt crack cocaine as a teenager before turning to rap at 21, meeting Jam Master Jay of Run-DMC who signed him and taught him to structure songs. He signed to Columbia Records and recorded Power of the Dollar, but was shot nine times in May 2000 and dropped from the label.
primary_leverage_engine: Street credibility and distribution through mixtapes
family_context_summary: Born to a single mother who was a drug dealer in Queens; mother was murdered when he was 8. Raised by grandparents in South Jamaica, Queens. No financial stability; began dealing drugs at age 12.
parent_family_domain_summary: No music industry background in family; mother was involved in drug dealing, which exposed him to street life but not to music or entertainment.
primary_early_advantage_tags: street life, Queens hip-hop scene, Jam Master Jay mentorship, G-Unit crew, mixtape distribution, adversity
evidence_summary: 50 Cent grew up in extreme adversity in South Jamaica, Queens: his drug-dealer mother was murdered when he was 8, and he was raised by grandparents while dealing crack by age 12. At 21 he met Jam Master Jay who taught him to rap and signed him to JMJ Records. He later signed to Columbia Records and recorded Power of the Dollar, with 'How to Rob' creating major industry buzz. He was shot nine times in May 2000 and dropped from Columbia, but rebuilt through mixtapes, leading to Eminem signing him in 2002.
starting_point: Born in Queens, New York to a single teenage mother who was a drug dealer; mother murdered when he was 8; raised by grandparents in South Jamaica, Queens in poverty.
current_position: Rapper, actor, and television producer; executive-produced and starred in Power (2014-2020) and spin-offs; estimated net worth ~$40M; resides in Houston, Texas.

trajectory.event: Signed to Columbia Records and recorded the album Power of the Dollar; single 'How to Rob' generated major industry buzz.
Shot nine times outside his grandmother's Queens home in May; dropped from Columbia Records; album release canceled.
Signed to Eminem's Shady Records after mixtape Guess Who's Back? was discovered; began recording Get Rich or Die Tryin'.
Released Get Rich or Die Tryin', which debuted at number one on Billboard 200 and sold over 12 million copies worldwide; launched G-Unit Records.
Released second album The Massacre, yielding number-one single 'Candy Shop'; continued massive commercial success.
Executive-produced and starred in the television series Power, launching a media empire through G-Unit Films and Television.

name: Astrud Gilberto
milestone_by_age_26: Recorded 'The Girl from Ipanema' for the Getz/Gilberto album in 1963 at age 23, which won a Grammy in 1965 and launched her solo career with The Astrud Gilberto Album in 1965.
early_history_summary: Born in Salvador, Bahia, to a German immigrant father who taught languages and a Brazilian mother who played instruments, Gilberto moved to Rio de Janeiro as a child. She married bossa nova creator João Gilberto in 1959 and was immersed in the bossa nova scene. She had no professional singing experience before being invited to sing English vocals on the Getz/Gilberto recording sessions in 1963.
primary_leverage_engine: Marriage into the bossa nova inner circle
family_context_summary: Born to a German immigrant father who was a language teacher and a Brazilian mother who played several instruments; middle-class family in Rio de Janeiro's Copacabana district.
parent_family_domain_summary: Mother played several instruments and ensured Astrud was musically educated; father was a language teacher (German and English), which gave Astrud multilingual ability that later proved crucial for 'The Girl from Ipanema.'
primary_early_advantage_tags: João Gilberto marriage, bossa nova epicenter, multilingual ability, musical family, Rio de Janeiro
evidence_summary: Astrud Gilberto was born in Salvador, Bahia, to a German language teacher father and a musically inclined Brazilian mother. The family moved to Rio's Copacabana in 1947, placing her at the epicenter of the emerging bossa nova scene. She married João Gilberto in 1959, gaining access to the inner circle of bossa nova including Tom Jobim and Vinicius de Moraes. Her father's English teaching gave her the language skills that led to her recording 'The Girl from Ipanema' in 1963, her professional singing debut. She had no prior professional experience but benefited from immersion in the bossa nova movement through her marriage and social circle.
starting_point: Born in Salvador, Bahia, Brazil, to a German immigrant father (language teacher) and a Brazilian mother who played several instruments; family relocated to Rio de Janeiro's Copacabana district in 1947.
current_position: Died on June 5, 2023, at age 83 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania; final albums released in 2002; retired from public performance in the early 2000s.

trajectory.event: Recorded 'The Girl from Ipanema' as her professional singing debut on the Getz/Gilberto album with Stan Getz and João Gilberto.
Getz/Gilberto album released; 'The Girl from Ipanema' became an international hit, reaching the US Top Five.
Won a Grammy for 'The Girl from Ipanema'; released her first solo album, The Astrud Gilberto Album, on Verve Records.
Divorced João Gilberto and began touring internationally with Stan Getz as a solo artist.
Released That Girl from Ipanema, incorporating disco elements into her bossa nova style.
Released her final album, Jungle, as the primary songwriter; retired from public performance thereafter.
Received the Latin Grammy Lifetime Achievement Award.
Died on June 5, 2023, in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania.

name: Kjetil André Aamodt
milestone_by_age_26: Won junior world championship titles in 1990 at age 18, then Olympic gold in super-G at Albertville 1992 at age 20, and World Championship golds in slalom and giant slalom in 1993.
early_history_summary: Born in Oslo, Norway, Aamodt grew up idolizing Swedish skiing legend Ingemar Stenmark. He made his FIS event debut at 15 in 1987 and World Cup debut at 16 in 1988. He won multiple gold medals at the 1990 World Junior Championships, then burst onto the senior scene with Olympic super-G gold at Albertville in 1992 at age 20, becoming Norway's first Alpine skiing Olympic champion in 40 years.
primary_leverage_engine: Physical talent and Norwegian skiing ecosystem
family_context_summary: Born in Oslo, Norway; family background not extensively documented in reviewed sources. Grew up in Norway's strong alpine skiing culture.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources; no evidence of family skiing background.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Norwegian skiing culture, early FIS debut, junior world champion, Olympic gold at 20, all-discipline versatility
evidence_summary: Aamodt was born in Oslo, Norway, and grew up in the country's dominant alpine skiing culture, idolizing Ingemar Stenmark. He made his FIS debut at 15 and World Cup debut at 16, showing exceptional early talent. He won multiple golds at the 1990 World Junior Championships at 18, then became Norway's first Alpine Olympic champion in 40 years with super-G gold at Albertville 1992 at age 20. His versatility across all disciplines was rare. Family background is not well documented, but Norway's skiing infrastructure provided a natural pipeline.
starting_point: Born in Oslo, Norway; family background not documented in reviewed sources; grew up in Norway's alpine skiing culture.
current_position: Retired from competitive skiing in January 2007 at age 35; works as a TV host and commentator; resides in Norway; most decorated Olympic alpine skier in history with 8 medals (4 gold).

trajectory.event: Won multiple gold medals at the World Junior Alpine Skiing Championships in Zinal, Switzerland, including downhill, super-G, and combined.
Won Olympic gold in super-G at Albertville, becoming Norway's first Alpine Olympic champion in 40 years and the discipline's youngest Olympic gold medalist.
Won World Championship golds in slalom and giant slalom, plus silver in combined; won first World Cup crystal globes for super-G and giant slalom.
Won the overall World Cup title and Olympic silver in downhill and combined at Lillehammer.
Won two Olympic gold medals at Salt Lake City in super-G and combined, cementing his status as an all-time great.
Won his fourth Olympic gold in super-G at Turin, extending his record as the most decorated Olympic alpine skier; retired in January 2007.

name: Petteri Nummelin
milestone_by_age_26: Won World Championship gold with Finland at the 1995 IIHF World Championships at age 22, and was an established professional in Sweden's top league (SHL) by his early twenties.
early_history_summary: Born in Turku, Finland, Nummelin is the son of Timo Nummelin, a Finnish ice hockey hall of famer and TPS icon. He grew up in his father's hockey environment, playing for TPS's junior program from age 16. He debuted in Finland's SM-Liiga at 19, won World Championship gold with Finland in 1995, then moved to Sweden's Frölunda and later Switzerland's Davos.
family_context_summary: Son of Timo Nummelin, a Finnish ice hockey hall of famer who played 23 seasons for TPS and represented Finland 225 times. Father's jersey number 3 was retired by TPS and passed to Petteri.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father Timo Nummelin was one of Finland's most iconic hockey players, a hall of famer who played for TPS for 23 seasons and represented Finland in eight World Championships. Petteri grew up immersed in hockey and inherited his father's position and jersey number at TPS.
primary_early_advantage_tags: father hockey hall of famer, TPS junior program, Finnish hockey culture, inherited jersey number, early national team
evidence_summary: Petteri Nummelin was born in Turku, Finland, as the son of Timo Nummelin, a Finnish hockey hall of famer who played 23 seasons for TPS and represented Finland 225 times. Petteri grew up in his father's hockey environment, joined TPS's junior program at 16, and debuted in the SM-Liiga at 19. He won Finland's first-ever World Championship gold in 1995 at age 22, then moved to Sweden's Frölunda and Switzerland's Davos. His father's legacy at TPS gave him direct access to elite hockey infrastructure and mentorship from childhood.
starting_point: Born in Turku, Finland, the son of Timo Nummelin, a Finnish ice hockey hall of famer and TPS icon; grew up immersed in hockey through his father's legacy.
current_position: Retired from professional hockey in 2019 after playing for PKS in Finland; inducted into the IIHF Hall of Fame in 2024; works as an assistant coach in Finnish hockey.

trajectory.event: Debuted in Finland's SM-Liiga with TPS and Reipas; also represented Finland at the World Junior Championships.
Won World Championship gold with Finland, the country's first-ever gold at the IIHF World Championships; signed with Frölunda in Sweden's top league.
Drafted 133rd overall by Columbus Blue Jackets and made NHL debut in the club's inaugural season.
Won the Swiss National League A scoring title as a defenseman with HC Lugano, a rare achievement.
Represented Finland at the Turin Olympics; returned to NHL with Minnesota Wild for two seasons.
Inducted into the IIHF Hall of Fame in recognition of 15 World Championship appearances and 104 career games.

name: Jan Gehl
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found; he had completed his M.Arch in 1960 and was practicing architecture, but his influential research and publications began only in 1965-1971.
early_history_summary: Gehl received his Masters of Architecture from the Royal Danish Academy of Fine Arts in 1960 and practiced architecture from 1960 to 1966. His first research grant came in 1965 at age 29, leading to studies of public spaces that culminated in his influential book Life Between Buildings (1971).
family_context_summary: Born in Copenhagen, Denmark; married Ingrid Gehl, a psychologist, who collaborated with him on early research into public spaces. Family financial background not documented.
evidence_summary: Gehl graduated with an M.Arch from KADK in 1960 and practiced architecture for six years. His career-defining work began with a research grant in 1965 at age 29, leading to the publication of Life Between Buildings in 1971 at age 35. No material, independently verifiable milestone occurred by age 26; he was a practicing architect with a standard degree.

name: Peter J. Ratcliffe
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found; he was in medical and clinical training during his twenties, with his research on oxygen sensing beginning only in the late 1980s and his first major discoveries in the 1990s.
early_history_summary: Ratcliffe studied medicine at Gonville and Caius College, Cambridge and St. Bartholomew's Hospital, London. He completed his MD research degree in 1987 and set up the Hypoxia Biology laboratory at Oxford in 1990. His Nobel Prize-winning work on oxygen sensing mechanisms came in the 1990s and 2000s.
family_context_summary: Grew up in northwest England; wanted to become a chemist as a teenager but was guided toward medicine. Family financial background not documented.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources; no evidence of family scientific or medical background.
evidence_summary: Ratcliffe trained in medicine at Cambridge and St. Bartholomew's, completing his MD in 1987. His oxygen-sensing research began at Oxford in 1990, with key discoveries in the 1990s leading to the 2019 Nobel Prize. By age 26 he was in clinical training with no notable research milestone.

name: Boško Abramović
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found; he was an active chess competitor but had not yet earned any formal title. His National Master title came in 1979 at age 28, International Master in 1980, and Grandmaster in 1984.
early_history_summary: Born in Zrenjanin, Yugoslavia, Abramović learned chess at age 11 and moved to Belgrade in 1970 at age 19 to pursue competitive chess. He developed gradually, earning National Master in 1979, International Master in 1980, and Grandmaster in 1984, with his first notable tournament results coming in 1979.
family_context_summary: Born in Zrenjanin, Yugoslavia (now Serbia); family background not documented in reviewed sources.
evidence_summary: Abramović learned chess at 11 and moved to Belgrade at 19 to compete seriously. He developed slowly, with his first formal title (National Master) coming at 28 in 1979. By age 26 he was an active competitor but had no titled achievement or notable tournament result. His Grandmaster title came in 1984 at age 33.

name: Pedro Almodóvar
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found; he was making amateur Super 8 short films shown in counter-culture circles, but his first feature film (Pepi, Luci, Bom) was not released until 1980 at age 31.
early_history_summary: Born in Calzada de Calatrava, Spain, Almodóvar moved to Madrid in 1968 and worked at the National Telephone Company while making Super 8 short films from 1972-1978. He was part of La Movida Madrileña counter-culture scene but had no professional film release until 1980.
family_context_summary: Born in a small rural town in La Mancha, Spain; father was a winemaker, mother was a letter reader and transcriber for illiterate neighbors. Not wealthy; could not afford film school.
parent_family_domain_summary: No film or artistic background in the family; father was a winemaker, mother read and wrote letters for illiterate neighbors.
evidence_summary: Almodóvar moved to Madrid in 1968, worked at the telephone company, and bought a Super 8 camera to make short films from 1972-1978. By age 26 (1975) he was making amateur shorts shown in counter-culture circles, but had no professional film credit. His first feature film, Pepi, Luci, Bom, was released in 1980 at age 31. Film schools were closed under Franco, blocking formal training.
